title: lore link writes the Story's tasks: frontmatter before the tracker back-reference can refuse, leaving the link half-applied
description:
`runLink` (src/commands/link.ts) calls `writeTasksIfChanged` -- which writes the concept's `tasks:` frontmatter to disk -- BEFORE the back-reference loop that calls `adapter.editTask`. If the tracker write refuses, the Story half is already committed to disk and the tracker knows nothing about the link.

REPORTED by opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-14, from a scratch probe rather than a suite row -- their harness sets `LORE_QUEST_*` at the process level, so no suite there has ever hit it. With no actor env set, `lore link` failed with `quest.actor-context-required` (exit 6), and afterwards `lore tasks <story>` already listed the task and the Story file's `tasks:` frontmatter already carried it.

CONFIRMED IN SOURCE, not just from the report: `const changed = writeTasksIfChanged(docsRoot, concept, existingTasks, nextTasks, profile)` runs at src/commands/link.ts:250; the `runSequentially` back-ref loop that can throw starts at :263. There is an up-front validation pass and its comment says 'Validate every task exists BEFORE any write' -- but it validates task EXISTENCE, not actor context, so the actor-context refusal surfaces only at `editTask`, after the Story write.

IMPORTANT NUANCE, so this is not over-stated: the failure is LOUD and RECOVERABLE, not silent corruption. The command exits 6, the report marks the task `backRef: "failed"` with a reason, and a re-run after fixing the actor env re-attempts the back-reference (the Story side then reads as already-linked). `lore check` should also see the resulting drift. So the cost is a half-applied state a human must notice and retry, not lost data.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS. The actor-context case is exactly where this bites hardest: a misconfigured CI hits it on EVERY invocation, so every run leaves the Story modified and the tracker untouched, and an unattended pipeline accumulates Story-side links no tracker record backs. That is the same shape as LCLI-492's finding -- a failure that is fine when a human is watching and compounds when nobody is.

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed, and the machinery already exists: `lore sync` solved the identical problem with `writeManyAtomicOrRollback` (LORE-120, src/commands/fswrite.ts), which undoes every write already applied in the same run if a later one throws. Either order the Story write AFTER the tracker write, or stage it and roll it back on refusal, or preflight the actor context alongside the existing task-existence validation so the refusal happens before any write. The third is cheapest and matches the comment that is already there.

CHECK `lore unlink` FOR THE SAME SHAPE -- `runUnlink` has the same two-phase structure and was not examined while filing this.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A `lore link` whose tracker back-reference refuses leaves the concept file BYTE-IDENTICAL to before the run — asserted on on-disk bytes, not on the exit code or the report.
The actor-context refusal specifically is covered, since that is the reported case and the one a misconfigured CI reproduces on every invocation.
`lore unlink` is checked for the same two-phase write ordering, and either fixed or explicitly cleared with the reason recorded.

Whichever approach is taken — preflight, reordering, or rollback — a partial back-ref failure across MULTIPLE task ids leaves a consistent state, since `runSequentially` can fail on the second id after the first succeeded.
A test is verified mutation-sensitive: reintroduce the early write and it must fail.
`bun run lint`, `typecheck` and the test suite pass, and `lore check` exits 0.

implementationNotes: DEDUPE PASS 2026-09-17 (OPAG-176): related to, not a duplicate of, LCLI-522. Both are lore-link tracker-write-safety defects in the same file (src/commands/link.ts), but different failure modes -- this task is about write-ORDERING (Story frontmatter written before the tracker back-reference can refuse), LCLI-522 is about a missing --if-revision precondition on a read-modify-write. Left as two records deliberately; each is independently actionable.
